**Estimate:** Coca-Cola sold about **DKK 104 million** in the **CSD / carbonated soft drinks** category in **Danish retail** in **January 2026**.

**Assumption:** I interpret “sell” as **retail sales value in DKK** for the Coca-Cola brand/trademark in Danish off-trade retail, not wholesale revenue or liters.

**Range:** **DKK 75 million–135 million**  
**Confidence:** **Low-to-moderate, ~35%** — public sources give market/category context, but not brand-level monthly scanner sales.

**Basis for estimate:** Denmark’s at-home soft drinks market is estimated by Statista at **US$1.39bn in 2025**, with at-home defined as retail channels such as supermarkets and convenience stores; carbonated soft drinks are the largest soft-drinks segment. ([statista.com](https://www.statista.com/outlook/cmo/non-alcoholic-drinks/soft-drinks/denmark?currency=usd&utm_source=openai)) Coca-Cola products in Denmark are produced/sold locally via Carlsberg’s system, and Carlsberg reported 2025 Danish soft-drink market volume growth of **3.9%** plus a **1.6 percentage-point** share gain in soda. ([coca-cola.com](https://www.coca-cola.com/dk/da/media-center/coca-cola-systemet-producerer-verdens-mest-populaere-drikkevare-i-fredericia)) I assumed CSD is roughly 60–65% of at-home soft-drink value, Coca-Cola’s brand value share in CSD around the high-20s percent after some 2025 pressure from local-brand substitution, and January at roughly 6–7% of annual sales due to seasonality. Euromonitor’s public summary also indicates Coca-Cola/Carlsberg remained a leading player but saw share pressure in 2025. ([euromonitor.com](https://www.euromonitor.com/carbonates-in-denmark/report?utm_source=openai))
